create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

saml.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry or revocation.
saml.note: Do not flag simple reuse of a valid access token as replay unless testing a one-time artifact.

saml.description: The nbf claim is optional and may be absent; acceptance of tokens without nbf is spec-compliant.
saml.note: Do not treat missing nbf as a vulnerability.

saml.description: The nbf claim is optional in JWTs and absence of nbf is not itself a vulnerability.
saml.note: Do not flag acceptance of tokens without nbf as a bug.

saml.description: JWKS keys may rotate without notice and clients are expected to cache and refresh keys.
saml.note: Acceptance of an old key during cache lifetime is normal JWKS behavior; only flag acceptance after expected refresh/expiry.

saml.description: Admin-configured trust anchor changes for identity providers or keys are by design and take effect for subsequent logins.
saml.note: Do not flag successful logins after an admin intentionally changed issuer, metadata, or signing keys.

saml.description: When an administrator reconfigures trust anchors, issuers, or signing keys, acceptance under the new configuration is expected behavior.
saml.note: Do not flag successful authentication after an admin-authorized trust change as trust-anchor substitution.

saml.description: Old signing keys may remain accepted until JWKS caches refresh after rotation.
saml.note: Do not flag acceptance of old keys before cache refresh/expiry as a trust-anchor violation.

saml.description: SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when authentication fails; failure is encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message.
saml.note: HTTP status alone is not a success oracle for SAML.

saml.description: When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, the returned ID token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This is RFC-conformant token exchange behavior, not a token confusion bug.

saml.description: Introspection only reports active=true when the introspecting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: An inactive introspection result from a non-audience client is expected and not evidence of revocation or invalid token issuance.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows when acting as a SAML identity provider.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are by design and should not be flagged as broken flow coherence.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. For SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST first initiate the flow against /saml/v2/SSO and preserve request state; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

The documented /saml/v2/SSO endpoint is ZITADEL acting as a SAML IdP, not a SAML ACS consumer. For target protocol saml against ZITADEL, saml_login MUST be modeled as initiating SSO at /saml/v2/SSO, not posting a forged SAMLResponse to ZITADEL. SAML IdP-broker tests that require ZITADEL to consume upstream SAML assertions need separate v2 SAML custom-login APIs not documented here as standard endpoints.

SAML /saml/v2/SSO error handling is by design HTTP 200 with failure encoded inside SAML StatusCode and message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 alone as successful authentication for SAML tests; it must inspect the returned SAMLResponse status.

For SAML signature-integrity tests against ZITADEL as IdP, the relevant verifier is the downstream SP, not ZITADEL. Attacks like saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, saml_no_conditions, and saml_wrong_audience do not target the documented /saml/v2/SSO behavior directly unless testing a separate ZITADEL broker-consumer flow.

When testing SAML-brokered login into OIDC applications, the fuzzer MUST complete the OIDC flow after browser authentication: start at /oauth/v2/authorize, then exchange the returned code at /oauth/v2/token, then inspect identity via /oidc/v1/userinfo. Without the OIDC completion steps, SAML login success cannot be verified in ZITADEL-issued tokens.

For I2 expired/future token controls on JWT-based token endpoint grants, JWT assertions used with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer or private_key_jwt MUST include aud containing the ZITADEL issuing domain and iat no older than 1 hour. A failed login without these fields may reflect malformed client authentication rather than freshness enforcement. Include a control assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}.

JWT client assertions and JWT profile grants require a kid header identifying the configured keyId. The fuzzer MUST include kid in JWT headers for private_key_jwt and service-account JWT profile tests; otherwise failures are ambiguous and do not prove signature validation behavior.

Token exchange audience is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 audience-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST first mint subject/actor tokens whose audiences include the target project/client; otherwise rejection is expected by design and not evidence of proper downstream audience enforcement.

Token exchange scope can differ from the input token and may be extended or decreased, but invalid_scope is returned when requested scope exceeds what ZITADEL allows. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare exchanged-token claims and scopes against upstream authorization and broker policy; do not assume any scope change is a bug.

Token exchange requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use session_token from such a response as a Bearer token for /userinfo or resource access; request an access token or JWT token type instead when subsequent API calls are needed.
Refresh tokens are not allowed as subject_token or actor_token in token exchange. Tests attempting refresh-token exchange are invalid on ZITADEL and resulting failures are by design.

The token introspection endpoint returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST introspect with a client/application that is in the token aud; otherwise inactive/authorization failure is expected and not evidence of revocation or freshness failure.

ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default. The fuzzer MUST treat access_token as an opaque bearer unless the application is explicitly configured for JWT access tokens or token exchange requested_token_type=jwt is used. Local JWT parsing assumptions will cause false negatives in identity and freshness checks.

For OIDC authorization requests, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. For replay-oriented tests involving id_token validation, the fuzzer SHOULD include nonce and verify it round-trips in the ID token when applicable; missing nonce in implicit flow is an invalid test setup.

If organization-specific login settings override defaults, the fuzzer MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} in the authorization request to force the intended organization context. Otherwise ZITADEL may apply default instance settings and select different external IdPs or policies, invalidating SAML-broker tests.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SAML flow first and preserve request state (including request ID / InResponseTo correlation) before evaluating any SAML response handling. IdP-initiated tests are invalid against this platform and will produce false positives for I3/I1.

For SAML brokering into ZITADEL Login V2, user creation can fail unless required user fields are mapped from upstream SAML attributes. The fuzzer MUST ensure upstream assertions include attributes sufficient to populate username/email/given_name/family_name, or configure an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. Otherwise failed login may reflect missing profile mapping, not a security rejection.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. The fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' on the instance default settings or target organization before testing SAML upstream login. Otherwise SAML login failures are expected policy behavior, not I1/I2/I3/I4/I5 findings.

If organization-specific settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} to select the target organization and its configured external IdPs. Without this scope, ZITADEL may use default settings and the wrong IdP set, causing false negatives/positives in SAML tests.

When testing I2 freshness on OIDC tokens obtained after SAML brokering, include a CONTROL login using a valid authorization flow and valid token exchange parameters. ZITADEL returns 401/invalid_client or invalid_grant for many setup/authentication mistakes, so an attack login failure without a control cannot distinguish security enforcement from broken client setup.

Token exchange scope behavior is permissive by design: requested scope can differ from supplied token scope, but invalid_scope is returned if it exceeds what ZITADEL allows. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual scope/claims to upstream authorization and broker policy; do not assume any scope change request is itself a violation.

Token exchange with requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned access_token field as a bearer API credential for verify_granted_identity or resource access. Use requested access_token/JWT types when a bearer token is needed.

For impersonation-style token exchange tests, actor_token is required for user_id and self-signed JWT subject_token modes, and the actor must hold impersonation permissions with instance security allowing impersonation. Without these prerequisites, rejection is expected and not evidence of I5 or I4 issues.

ZITADEL introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST introspect with a client/application that is in the token audience; otherwise active=false is expected and must not be misread as token revocation or freshness failure.

JWT client assertions used on token or introspection endpoints require aud to include ZITADEL's issuing domain, iat not older than 1 hour, and a kid header matching the registered keyId. Failures from violating these requirements are setup errors, not security rejections under test.

JWKS and signing keys are rotated and may be cached by clients. For any trust-anchor rotation test involving ZITADEL-issued JWT validation, acceptance of an old key before cache refresh is standard caching behavior; only acceptance after cache expiry should be considered suspicious.

For SAML tests against ZITADEL as broker/SP, user creation in Login V2 can fail unless required fields are mapped from SAML attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST ensure the upstream SAML assertion provides required attributes (at least email, first name, last name, and identifier) or treat user-creation failure as setup failure, not a security oracle.

When testing SAML provider setup, external IdP login must be allowed in the login policy. If External Login allowed is disabled, SAML authentication will fail by policy and MUST NOT be interpreted as a security rejection.

SAML SSO endpoint error handling is protocol-level: HTTP status may still be 200 even when authentication failed, with failure encoded in SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT rely on HTTP 2xx alone as success for /saml/v2/SSO responses.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, ZITADEL documentation states SAML assertions/responses are signed and the SP/ACS must validate signatures, issuer, destination, audience, recipient, and validity window. The fuzzer MUST craft attacks against the SAMLResponse content, not assume transport-level HTTP status alone proves signature acceptance.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay tests, ZITADEL documentation explicitly recommends using a historical cache to track and reject duplicate IDs. The fuzzer SHOULD replay the exact same assertion identifier and treat acceptance as a replay weakness.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion and I5 audience/conditions tests, the fuzzer MUST include a control login with a valid assertion first. Otherwise a failed SAML flow may be caused by missing attribute mapping, disabled external login, or general setup issues rather than enforcement of Conditions.
OIDC authorization requests used to reach SAML brokering MUST include scope=openid. Missing openid causes invalid_scope and breaks the brokered login setup.

For OIDC code-flow sequences around SAML brokering, redirect_uri must exactly match a preregistered URI and the token exchange redirect_uri must exactly match the authorization request redirect_uri. Mismatches produce invalid_grant/authorization failure and are setup errors, not security outcomes.

For I2 nonce-related OIDC SSO tests, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended for code flow to bind client session to the ID token. The fuzzer SHOULD send nonce on authorization requests and MUST treat missing nonce validation only in the RP/id_token context, not in plain SAML upstream assertions.

Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST introspect with a client that is in the token audience; otherwise inactive/401 results are by design and not evidence of token invalidity.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. Rejection of a broader audience is by design and MUST NOT be flagged as a bug.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, ZITADEL allows scope to change during token exchange but validates it. The fuzzer MUST compare granted scope in the response, not just requested scope, and treat narrowing or rejection as correct behavior.

For token exchange, the access_token response field may contain a non-access token when requested_token_type=id_token, and token_type will be N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use such a returned value as Bearer session_token for subsequent API calls.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT profile or private_key_jwt client assertions, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Failures caused by violating these client-auth requirements are setup errors, not broker vulnerabilities.

For JWT profile grants and private_key_jwt authentication, the JWT header kid is required to identify the key. Omitting or altering kid can cause expected rejection unrelated to the invariant under test.

Reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization. For multi-org SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this scope narrowing behavior; login failure under the wrong org scope is by design.

If organization-specific settings override default settings, the fuzzer MUST send the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} in the OIDC authorization request to exercise the intended org-specific SAML provider and login policy. Otherwise tests may hit default settings and misinterpret results.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
